teaching.explanationEs: No way! expresa sorpresa; had never heard: algo que no habías oído hasta ahora.
teaching.audioText: No way! I had never heard that story before.

prompt.es: Elige la mejor reacción a la historia de tu amigo.

choices.text: I used to swim every day.
Where did you used to swim?

feedback.es: Una buena reacción muestra interés (Oh no!) y pide seguir con una pregunta de seguimiento en pasado.

hint.es: Reacciona y pregunta qué pasó después.

origin.text: Friend: While we were swimming, a storm suddenly began.

prompt.es: Completa: «¿Cómo te sentiste cuando empezó la tormenta?»

answer.text: feel

feedback.es: Después de did el verbo va en forma base: How did you feel, no How did you felt.

hint.es: Después de did va el verbo base.

origin.text: How did you ___ when the storm began?

prompt.es: Ordena: «Suena muy aterrador.»

answer.text: That sounds really scary

feedback.es: That sounds + adjetivo reacciona a una historia; really refuerza el adjetivo.

prompt.es: Escucha el recuerdo y elige la pregunta de seguimiento que encaja.

choices.text: What did you do when the storm began?
What did you do when the boat moved?
What did you do when the lights went out?

feedback.es: En el recuerdo se apagaron las luces mientras cocinaban: la pregunta de seguimiento natural retoma ese hecho, no una tormenta ni un barco.

origin.audio: When I was small, I used to visit my grandmother every Saturday. One day, while we were cooking, the lights went out.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con lo que hace en la conversación.

pairs: No way!
That sounds amazing!
What happened next?
How did you feel?

feedback.es: Reaccionar y preguntar mantiene viva la conversación: cada frase tiene una función distinta.

pairs: No way!
That sounds amazing!
What happened next?
How did you feel?

prompt.es: Completa: «Suena muy gracioso. ¿Qué hiciste después de eso?»

answer.text: sounds | did

feedback.es: That sounds + adjetivo reacciona a la historia; What did you do pregunta por lo que hizo la persona.

prompt.es: Reacciona al recuerdo de Ana, cuenta uno tuyo y haz dos preguntas.

answer.text: Wow, that sounds amazing! When I was small, I used to go to the park with my grandfather. One day, while we were walking there, it suddenly started to rain, and it was really funny. What happened next in your story? And how did you feel?
accepted: Wow, that sounds amazing! When I was small, I used to go to the park with my grandfather. One day, while we were walking there, it suddenly started to rain, and it was really funny. What happened next in your story? And how did you feel?

Really? That sounds funny! When I was ten, I would visit my grandmother every Saturday. One day, while we were cooking, the lights suddenly went out, and it was really scary. What happened next? How did you feel when you saw the fish?

No way! That sounds amazing! When I was a child, I used to play in the street every afternoon. One day, while I was playing, I found a wallet, and I was really happy. What did you do next? And were you scared?

feedback.es: Una buena respuesta reacciona (That sounds amazing), cuenta un recuerdo con hábito y escena, y pregunta en pasado: What happened next? How did you feel?

origin.text: Ana te cuenta: «Cuando era pequeña, solía ir al lago con mi abuelo. Un día, mientras pescábamos, vi un pez enorme.» Reacciona con entusiasmo, cuenta un recuerdo tuyo de infancia (un hábito y un día en que algo pasó mientras hacías otra cosa) y haz dos preguntas: qué pasó después y cómo se sintió.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo se sintió la hablante.

feedback.es: La hablante termina con «I had never been so scared!»: se asustó muchísimo.

origin.audio: When I was nine, we used to visit a lake every August. One day, while we were swimming, our boat suddenly moved away. I had never been so scared!

prompt.es: Completa: «¡No puede ser! Nunca había oído esa historia.»

answer.text: No

feedback.es: No way! es una forma natural de expresar sorpresa ante una historia.

origin.text: ___ way! I had never heard that story before.

prompt.es: ¿Qué pregunta de seguimiento encaja con lo que cuenta Leo?

choices.text: How did you felt when it happened?
How did you feel when it happened?
How you did feel when it happened?

feedback.es: Después de did va el verbo base (feel) y el orden es How + did + you.

origin.text: Leo: One day, while we were walking home, I found a wallet.

prompt.es: ¿Qué reacción de seguimiento es más natural?

choices.text: I used to sleep with a light.
Really? What did you do then?

feedback.es: Really? muestra interés y What did you do then? invita a seguir la historia del apagón.

origin.text: Sara: When I was eight, I used to sleep with a light on. One night, while I was sleeping, the light went out.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué opina la hablante de la historia de su hermano.

feedback.es: «It was really funny» dice que disfrutó la historia de su hermano.

origin.audio: Yesterday my brother told me a story about his old school, and it was really funny!

prompt.es: Ordena: «¡Ay, no! ¿Qué hiciste después?»

answer.text: Oh no what did you do next

feedback.es: Oh no reacciona y What did you do next? pregunta en pasado por lo que hizo después.
